# Elm of Hospice (`elm-of-hospice`)

Hospice room and board for nursing-home residents: hospice days not invoiced to the hospice, invoiced days not on the census, invoices below the contract rate, unpaid invoices past terms, hospices with no contract and Medicaid billed directly for hospice days. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Elm never sends invoices or statements to a hospice.**

Evergreen ver 1 · Billing and revenue cycle · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`evergreen-core`](../evergreen-core)

```bash
npx -y elm-of-hospice demo
npx -y elm-of-hospice mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow hospice residents for March 2026, reviewed on 20 April. Planted:

- R1101: invoiced in full at the contract rate and paid. Nothing to fix.
- R1102: invoiced only to 20 March, at 180 a day against a 195 contract rate.
- R1103: on Prairie Light Hospice, which has no contract, and not invoiced.
- R1104: invoiced to a hospice but not a hospice resident on the census.
- R1105: on hospice until discharge on 21 March, with no March invoice, a February invoice unpaid for 50 days, and 15 to 20 March also billed to Medicaid.

[`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `elm_check` | Compare hospice census days, room and board invoices, contracts and Medicaid claims for a month. | runs |
| `elm_write_report` | Write elm-hospice.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and elm-hospice.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/elm). | runs |
| `elm_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `elm_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `elm_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `elm_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `hospice_invoice_send` | Elm never sends invoices or statements to a hospice. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `elm_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `census` (required) | Census under --root, with a Hospice column or hospice payer rows |
| `invoices` (required) | Room and board invoices to hospices under --root: resident, hospice, service dates, days, amount, invoice date, paid amount |
| `contracts` (required) | Hospice contracts under --root: hospice, daily rate, effective dates, payment terms |
| `claims` | Optional Medicaid claim lines under --root, to catch hospice days billed to Medicaid directly |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: pay_days |
| `month` (required) | Month to check, YYYY-MM |
| `as_of` | Date to age unpaid invoices from (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx elm-of-hospice inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Census (`census`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Facility Name, Building, Location, Fac, Center |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Census Date |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `bed_status` | text | Bed Status, Status, Census Status, Action, Census Action, Leave Type |

| `hospice` | text | Hospice, Hospice Provider, Hospice Agency, Hospice Name |

## Settings file (`elm_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pay_days` | Days a hospice has to pay when the contract does not say (default 30) |

## Memory

`elm_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `elm_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `hospice_alias` | is listed with results so staff can fix the census or contract file. It never changes a check by itself. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `evergreen-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "elm-of-hospice": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "elm-of-hospice",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add elm-of-hospice -- npx -y elm-of-hospice mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
elm-of-hospice tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
elm-of-hospice sources               # the columns each input is read from
elm-of-hospice inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
elm-of-hospice call elm_check '{"census":"<census>","invoices":"<invoices>","contracts":"<contracts>","month":"<month>"}'
elm-of-hospice eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
elm-of-hospice demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
